packet.headline_seed: News live: Marles says Australia has expressed concern over China missile test as Taiwan criticises ‘provocation’
packet.description_seed: Wong says missile test in Pacific a ‘destabilising act’ that could ‘lead to miscalculation’. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Marles said he doubts China tested the long-range weapon yesterday in response to Anthony Albanese being in the Pacific to sign a new defence alliance with Fiji, but said Australia remains deeply concerned by the development. He told ABC News: At the end of the day, what we’re seeing here is a long-range missile test from China, which China itself has said is nuclear capable … This is China demonstrating a much greater range in terms of being able to deploy a nuclear weapon. And ultimately what that is, is deeply destabilising. Our fundamental issue in relation to China is that we have seen a very dramatic military buildup by China without that strategic reassurance [to our neighbours]. There really isn’t an explanation as to why they are building the capabilities that they are and that is fundamentally destabilising. I think the system is handling the matter as it should … I think it’s appropriate that the legal process takes its course. Continue reading...

clean_source_blocks.text: Wong says missile test in Pacific a ‘destabilising act’ that could ‘lead to miscalculation’. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Marles said he doubts China tested the long-range weapon yesterday in response to Anthony Albanese being in the Pacific to sign a new defence alliance with Fiji, but said Australia remains deeply concerned by the development. He told ABC News: At the end of the day, what we’re seeing here is a long-range missile test from China, which China itself has said is nuclear capable … This is China demonstrating a much greater range in terms of being able to deploy a nuclear weapon. And ultimately what that is, is deeply destabilising. Our fundamental issue in relation to China is that we have seen a very dramatic military buildup by China without that strategic reassurance [to our neighbours]. There really isn’t an explanation as to why they are building the capabilities that they are and that is fundamentally destabilising. I think the system is handling the matter as it should … I think it’s appropriate that the legal process takes its course. Continue reading...

Pat Conroy, the defence industry minister, spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, saying the Chinese government had been planning to test a long-range missile for “some time” but only informed the Australian government a few hours beforehand. We’ve been very clear that we’re seeing the biggest military buildup in our region since World War II and it’s not being accompanied by sufficient transparency. Conroy said he believes the launch was “more likely to be a coincidence rather than linked” to Australia’s defence agreements with Fiji yesterday. But he added that was “obviously” a question for the Chinese government. He went on: This is something that can destabilise the region but it doesn’t take away from our efforts to implement what the Pacific leaders have called for, which is Pacific security to come from within the Pacific.

"We have much to transact, so we look forward to great conversations," he said. Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong says China's test of a nuclear-capable missile is counter to the Pacific leaders' requests for peace in the region. The long-range missile was launched yesterday from a Chinese submarine, landing in the ocean around 1,000 kilometres north-east of the Solomon Islands. Speaking to ABC's AM program, Wong says she'll let China explain its intent in conducting the test. "I'll simply indicate that Australia's view is this test is destabilising for the region and raises the risk of miscalculation," she says. "We do not believe this test is consistent with the view that Pacific leaders have very clearly expressed that the Pacific should be an Ocean of Peace."

Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy says Australia was monitoring a Chinese navy task force group that was involved in tracking a long-range missile test. Follow all the updates in our live blog. Choose what information you see below by using filters Anthony Albanese and his Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale have held a quick bilateral meeting at Honiara airport just hours after Albanese's arrival. Albanese told Wale that there was "much more that we need to do together", including "the development of a comprehensive treaty". "We will task our ministers to continue to do work on that and hopefully to conclude that by the end of the year," the prime minister said. Wale said he was "extremely pleased" to see Albanese so soon after his own visit to Canberra in early June.

payload.title: Australia arvostelee Kiinan ohjuskoetta Tyynellämerellä
payload.summary: Australia on ilmaissut huolensa Kiinan pitkän kantaman ohjuskokeesta Tyynellämerellä. Maan ulkoministeri Penny Wongin mukaan koe horjuttaa alueen vakautta ja voi lisätä virhearvioiden riskiä.
payload.content:
Australia on arvostellut Kiinan Tyynellämerellä tekemää pitkän kantaman ohjuskoetta ja pitää sitä alueen vakautta horjuttavana toimena. Australian viranomaisten mukaan Kiina ilmoitti kokeesta vain muutamia tunteja etukäteen, vaikka ohjus oli maan omien tietojen mukaan ydinkykyinen ja se laukaistiin kiinalaisesta sukellusveneestä.

## Ohjus putosi lähelle Salomonsaaria

Australian ulkoministeri Penny Wong sanoi, että Kiinan koe ei vastaa Tyynenmeren johtajien esittämää tavoitetta rauhanomaisesta alueesta. Hänen mukaansa Australian näkemys on, että koe lisää virhearvioiden riskiä.

ABC:n mukaan pitkän kantaman ohjus laukaistiin kiinalaisesta sukellusveneestä ja se päätyi mereen noin 1 000 kilometriä Salomonsaarten koillispuolelle. Wong sanoi jättävänsä Kiinan selitettäväksi, mikä kokeen tarkoitus oli.

Australian puolustusministeri Richard Marles kuvasi koetta syvästi huolestuttavaksi. Hänen mukaansa kyse on Kiinan kyvystä osoittaa aiempaa pidempää kantamaa ydinasetta varten. Marles sanoi myös, että Australian keskeinen huoli liittyy Kiinan nopeaan sotilaalliseen varustautumiseen, jota ei hänen mukaansa ole seurannut riittävä strateginen avoimuus alueen naapureille.

## Canberra pitää ajoitusta todennäköisesti sattumana

Puolustusteollisuusministeri Pat Conroy sanoi, että Kiinan hallinto oli suunnitellut koetta jo jonkin aikaa, mutta ilmoitti siitä Australialle vasta muutamia tunteja ennen laukaisua. Hänen mukaansa Australia seurasi Kiinan laivaston osastoa, joka oli mukana ohjuskokeen tarkkailussa.

Conroyn mukaan laukaisu oli todennäköisemmin sattumaa kuin suoraan yhteydessä Australian tuoreisiin puolustusjärjestelyihin Tyynellämerellä. Australian pääministeri Anthony Albanese oli samaan aikaan alueella, missä Australia oli edistämässä puolustusyhteistyötä Fidžin kanssa.

Albanese tapasi myös Salomonsaarten pääministerin Matthew Walen Honiaran lentokentällä pian saavuttuaan maahan. Albanesen mukaan maiden välillä on vielä paljon tehtävää, mukaan lukien kattavan sopimuksen valmistelu. Hänen mukaansa ministereille annetaan tehtäväksi jatkaa työtä, jotta sopimus voitaisiin saada valmiiksi vuoden loppuun mennessä.

Australian hallituksen viesti on, että Kiinan ohjuskoe ei muuta sen pyrkimystä vahvistaa Tyynenmeren turvallisuutta alueen omista lähtökohdista.

Conroyn mukaan laukaisu oli todennäköisemmin sattumaa kuin suoraan yhteydessä Australian tuoreisiin puolustusjärjestelyihin Tyynellämerellä. Australian pääministeri Anthony Albanese oli samaan aikaan alueella, missä Australia oli edistämässä puolustusyhteistyötä Fidžin kanssa.

Albanese tapasi myös Salomonsaarten pääministerin Matthew Walen Honiaran lentokentällä pian saavuttuaan maahan. Albanesen mukaan maiden välillä on vielä paljon tehtävää, mukaan lukien kattavan sopimuksen valmistelu. Hänen mukaansa ministereille annetaan tehtäväksi jatkaa työtä, jotta sopimus voitaisiin saada valmiiksi vuoden loppuun mennessä.

Australian hallituksen viesti on, että Kiinan ohjuskoe ei muuta sen pyrkimystä vahvistaa Tyynenmeren turvallisuutta alueen omista lähtökohdista.

He told ABC News: At the end of the day, what we’re seeing here is a long-range missile test from China, which China itself has said is nuclear capable … This is China demonstrating a much greater range in terms of being able to deploy a nuclear weapon. And ultimately what that is, is deeply destabilising. Our fundamental issue in relation to China is that we have seen a very dramatic military buildup by China without that strategic reassurance [to our neighbours]. There really isn’t an explanation as to why they are building the capabilities that they are and that is fundamentally destabilising. I think the system is handling the matter as it should … I think it’s appropriate that the legal process takes its course. Continue reading...

Pat Conroy, the defence industry minister, spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, saying the Chinese government had been planning to test a long-range missile for “some time” but only informed the Australian government a few hours beforehand. We’ve been very clear that we’re seeing the biggest military buildup in our region since World War II and it’s not being accompanied by sufficient transparency. Conroy said he believes the launch was “more likely to be a coincidence rather than linked” to Australia’s defence agreements with Fiji yesterday. But he added that was “obviously” a question for the Chinese government. He went on: This is something that can destabilise the region but it doesn’t take away from our efforts to implement what the Pacific leaders have called for, which is Pacific security to come from within the Pacific.

"We have much to transact, so we look forward to great conversations," he said. Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong says China's test of a nuclear-capable missile is counter to the Pacific leaders' requests for peace in the region. The long-range missile was launched yesterday from a Chinese submarine, landing in the ocean around 1,000 kilometres north-east of the Solomon Islands. Speaking to ABC's AM program, Wong says she'll let China explain its intent in conducting the test. "I'll simply indicate that Australia's view is this test is destabilising for the region and raises the risk of miscalculation," she says. "We do not believe this test is consistent with the view that Pacific leaders have very clearly expressed that the Pacific should be an Ocean of Peace."
